podcast.title: Death (January 2025) – Cardiac Arrest at 78, Aggravated by Emphysema and California Wildfires
podcast.body: Filmmaker and musician David Lynch died at age 78 of cardiac arrest, a condition aggravated by emphysema and the California wildfires. As a musician, he produced the influential album *Floating Into the Night* by Julee Cruise. "Died at 78 of a cardiac arrest aggravated by emphysema and the California wildfires."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: "Twin Peaks" Soundtrack Collaboration
podcast.body: Lynch's collaboration with composer Angelo Badalamenti and singer Julee Cruise, which began with "Blue Velvet," extended to the TV series "Twin Peaks." He had a specific dreamy and spooky atmosphere in mind for the show, which they helped bring to life through its soundtrack.

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Failed Song Licensing for "Blue Velvet"
podcast.body: For his 1986 film "Blue Velvet," Lynch attempted to license "Song to the Siren" by This Mortal Coil from 4AD, but the label refused. This led him to collaborate with Angelo Badalamenti and Julee Cruise for the film's soundtrack.

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Floating Into the Night – Julee Cruise Production
podcast.body: Lynch produced this album for singer Julee Cruise, which is described as influential. "He produced the influential album 'Floating Into the Night' by Julee Cruise."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Formation of The Original Platters
podcast.body: After leaving The Platters in 1967, David Lynch formed a group called "The Original Platters," and recruited former classic lineup members Zola Taylor and Paul Robi to join him. "After David Lynch left in 1967, for example, he formed a group called The Original Platters, and got both Zola Taylor and Paul Roby into the group."

srcs.source: A History of Rock Music in 500 Songs

podcast.title: Interest in British Dreampop
podcast.body: By the time his film "Blue Velvet" was released in 1986, David Lynch was already a fan of British Dreampop. This interest informed the "dreamy, spooky atmosphere" he sought for his film and later for his TV series "Twin Peaks."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Association with David Lynch and Twin Peaks
xref.body: Julee Cruise gained prominence in the 1990s through her extensive musical contributions to director David Lynch's Twin Peaks projects, with her music featured throughout the TV series. "Julie had a nice run in the 1990s thanks to her association with director David Lynch and specifically his Twin Peaks projects. Her music was all over those TV series."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: In Memoriam of Those Lost in 2022

xref.title: Blue Velvet and Twin Peaks Collaboration
xref.body: Angelo Badalamenti collaborated with David Lynch, composing very dreamy songs for Lynch's 1986 film "Blue Velvet" and continuing their partnership for the "Twin Peaks" TV series. This collaboration was initiated after Lynch's attempt to license an existing Dreampop track failed.

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Collaboration with David Lynch
xref.body: Julee Cruise's singular major hit, "Falling," was a result of her collaboration with filmmaker David Lynch. Lynch commissioned the instrumental version for his TV series "Twin Peaks" and subsequently had Cruise record the vocal rendition. "He needed something appropriately surreal for the 1989 TV show Twin Peaks. He commissioned songwriter Angela Battlemente, who created an instrumental falling."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
